title: Torsors under finite locally constant sheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal G$ be a finite locally constant sheaf of groups on $\et X$
and let $P$ be a $\mathcal G$-torsor [def-constructible-torsor]. Then $P$ is trivial on an étale
cover of $X$.

external.place: A $G_X$-torsor is representable by a scheme $P\to X$ finite étale (locally on $X$ it is $\bigsqcup_{g\in G}X$, and the transition functions are locally constant permutations; see SGA 4); since $P\to X$ is étale and surjective it is an étale cover, and $P$ restricted to $P$ has the tautological section, so it is trivial there.

proof.text: Applying condition (2) of the torsor definition to U = X gives an etale covering \{U_i \to X\} such that P(U_i) is nonempty for every i.

Choose s_i in P(U_i). For every etale V \to U_i, the map G(V) \to P(V), g \mapsto g.s_i|_V, is bijective: the restriction s_i|_V is a section, so P(V) is nonempty, and simple transitivity gives existence and uniqueness of the required g for each section of P(V). These maps are compatible with restriction in V and with the G-action, hence define an isomorphism of G|_{U_i}-torsors from G|_{U_i} with left translation to P|_{U_i}. Thus P is trivial on the etale cover \{U_i \to X\}.

source.place: Definition 03AH, label definition-torsor, condition (1) and trivial torsor clause
